routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica Tracker: 2027 News and Facts
routes.description: Track official Resident Evil Veronica updates, sourced from Capcom and official Steam, PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo store listings.
routes.intro: Resident Evil Veronica is Capcom's official remake of the 2000 classic, confirmed for a 2027 release window on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2 and PC.
body: Capcom officially describes the project as a reimagining of Resident Evil Code: Veronica, updating the original foundation with modernized gameplay mechanics and more detailed graphics. The remake has a confirmed 2027 release window across PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC via Steam.
Official store links point readers to the Steam, PlayStation, Xbox and Nintendo listings; availability and regional visibility can vary by platform.

Capcom reported that the title passed one million combined wishlists across PS5 and PC shortly after its initial announcement, though an exact release date, launch pricing, product editions, preorders and a playable demo have not been announced.

Developer interviews report a modern third-person camera direction and involvement from members of the Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 4 remake development teams. PlayStation Blog coverage also notes that elements of the classic narrative will be adjusted to better align with the broader series lore established since 2000.

Technical specifications remain unconfirmed. While the Steam product page is live, minimum and recommended PC hardware requirements are listed as to be determined, with further platform details pending future Capcom announcements.

routes.title: バイオハザード ヴェロニカ 非公式情報トラッカー
routes.description: 『バイオハザード ヴェロニカ』リメイクの公式情報を追跡。カプコンの発表や各ストア情報に基づく発売時期、対応機種、最新事実をまとめています。
routes.h1: バイオハザード ヴェロニカ 情報トラッカー
routes.intro: 『バイオハザード ヴェロニカ』は2000年の名作を現代向けに再構築したカプコン公式リメイク作品で、2027年の発売が予定されています。
body: 本作は2000年に発売された『バイオハザード CODE:Veronica』を原作とし、現代的なゲームプレイとより緻密なグラフィックで再構築する公式リメイク作品です。発売時期は2027年予定で、対応プラットフォームはPlayStation 5、Xbox Series X|S、Nintendo Switch 2、PC（Steam）が発表されています。

Steam、PlayStation、Xbox、Nintendoの各公式ストアページが公開されており、Steamではウィッシュリスト登録が可能です。プロデューサーのインタビューでは三人称視点での進行や『バイオハザード RE:2』『バイオハザード RE:4』を手がけた制作陣の関与が報じられているほか、PlayStation Blogでは2000年以降に構築されたシリーズの公式設定に合わせて一部の物語調整が行われると言及されています。
物語の背景としてアルバート・ウェスカーの名が語られているものの、具体的な登場規模やプレイアブルキャラクターの確定発表ではありません。また、正確な発売日、販売価格、予約開始日、体験版の配信、限定版の仕様、PC版の動作環境（TBD）などの詳細は現時点で未公表となっており、公式発表があり次第更新します。

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica Release Date: 2027 Status
routes.description: Resident Evil Veronica is officially confirmed for 2027. Capcom has not announced an exact date, preorder date or launch price.
routes.intro: Capcom has officially confirmed a 2027 release window for Resident Evil Veronica, but an exact launch date has not been announced.
body: Capcom and official store listings place Resident Evil Veronica in a 2027 release window. None currently lists a season, month or day.
An exact release date, preorder date and launch price have not been announced.
Retailer placeholders, countdown pages and social posts are not release-date confirmation. Treat a date as official only when it appears in Capcom material or a matching official store update.
Wishlisting is available on several stores, but a wishlist button does not mean preorders are open.
A release window is not a launch date. The confirmed information currently stops at the year, so quarter, month and day claims need a dated Capcom announcement or matching official-store update.
Treat announcement, exact-date reveal, preorder opening and launch as separate events. The announcement and store wishlists are live; the exact date and preorder checkout are not confirmed.

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica Platforms: PS5, Xbox, Switch 2, PC
routes.description: Resident Evil Veronica is confirmed for PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC. Compare store features and unannounced details.
routes.intro: Resident Evil Veronica is officially confirmed for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC, with official store pages live across all four ecosystems.
body: Capcom has formally announced Resident Evil Veronica for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC via Steam. Official product pages are currently live across each digital storefront, allowing players to add the game to their wishlists ahead of launch.

The PlayStation listing currently shows offline single-player, DualSense vibration and trigger support, PS5 Pro enhancement and Game Help. The Xbox listing shows single-player, cloud saves, achievements, 4K Ultra HD and Series X|S optimization; these flags do not confirm a 4K or 60 FPS target. The Nintendo listing confirms a digital Switch 2 version with one local player and TV, tabletop and handheld modes.

On Steam, the listing confirms store fields such as achievements, Family Sharing, HDR, subtitles and support for fourteen languages. Capcom also reported more than one million combined PS5 and PC wishlists shortly after announcement, but wishlist milestones indicate interest rather than sales, preorder numbers or an exact launch date.

Metadata across platforms still contains temporary discrepancies. The Xbox listing shows a Mature 17+ badge and content descriptors while simultaneously noting that the title is not yet rated, leaving final age certification unresolved. Steam hardware requirements also remain listed as to be determined.

Capcom has not announced releases for older-generation consoles, cloud gaming services or subscription libraries. Physical editions, cross-save, regional timing, performance modes, target resolution and frame-rate details remain unconfirmed across the four platforms.

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica Trailer: Official Video Updates
routes.description: Watch official Resident Evil Veronica trailers. We track videos from Capcom, PlayStation, Xbox and Summer Game Fest to document settings and characters.
routes.h1: Resident Evil Veronica Trailers and Videos
routes.intro: Official Resident Evil Veronica trailers showcase the game's atmosphere, settings and characters, but they do not confirm every gameplay mechanic.
body: To ensure accuracy, this tracker covers verified video uploads. It monitors the official Resident Evil YouTube channel, regional Capcom accounts, PlayStation, Xbox and Summer Game Fest channels for authentic promotional material.

Promotional videos can reveal the general atmosphere, key settings and character designs, but a trailer cannot prove the inclusion of all mechanics, enemies, puzzles or specific story chapters. Curated footage represents a snapshot of the game rather than the complete gameplay experience.

Based on producer interviews and media coverage, the remake is reported to be a third-person title. Until Capcom publishes more comprehensive gameplay demonstrations, fans should rely on what is explicitly shown in official video feeds rather than drawing conclusions about unannounced gameplay systems.

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica Story: Official Premise Details
routes.description: Explore the official Resident Evil Veronica story premise. Claire searches for Chris in a survival-horror setting three months after Raccoon City.
routes.intro: The Resident Evil Veronica remake follows Claire Redfield to Rockfort Island three months after the biological disaster in Raccoon City.
body: According to the official Steam listing, the overarching narrative takes place three months after the devastating events in Raccoon City. Claire travels to France in search of her missing brother, Chris. Her investigation is cut short when she is captured by Umbrella special forces and transported to Rockfort Island.
The official game synopsis says that another biological disaster transforms Rockfort Island into a survival-horror setting.

The producer has stated that the remake will explore more of Claire's motivations. PlayStation Blog coverage also reports that parts of the original story will be adjusted to connect with the wider Resident Evil lore established since 2000.

The core premise is confirmed, but exact scenes, specific character arcs, puzzles, enemies, bosses and other detailed story changes remain unannounced. This page stays spoiler-light and updates only when official material clarifies more of the remake.

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica Characters: Cast Updates
routes.description: Track Resident Evil Veronica character information: Claire Redfield and Chris in the official premise, plus reported Wesker context.
routes.intro: Claire Redfield is the central focus of the Resident Evil Veronica remake, while the full cast and playable roster remain unannounced.
body: According to the official Steam premise, Claire Redfield is the primary focus of the story as she searches for her missing brother. Chris Redfield is named in this core narrative setup, but Capcom has not detailed the extent of his role, screen time or playability in the remake.

During story discussions, producer Yoshiaki Hirabayashi mentioned Albert Wesker alongside Claire and Chris. This narrative context should not be treated as a formal cast announcement or a playable-character reveal.
Individuals known only from the original 2000 release remain part of the classic-game context. Until Capcom formally confirms them in the remake, their return remains unconfirmed.

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica FAQ: Verified Facts
routes.description: Verified answers about the Resident Evil Veronica remake, based on Capcom announcements, official store pages and attributed producer interviews.
routes.intro: Read clear answers about the Resident Evil Veronica remake, with confirmed, reported and unknown details kept separate.
body: This independent tracker separates confirmed facts from speculation by relying on Capcom announcements, active digital storefronts and attributed producer interviews.
Details are labeled confirmed when backed by direct publisher or store data, reported when discussed in attributed interviews, and unknown when official sources have not clarified them.
Placeholder dates, retailer claims and community rumors are not confirmation. When an official source changes, the detailed topic page and dated changelog are updated before the short answer here.

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica Sources: Fact Verification
routes.description: Review the official sources and verification hierarchy behind Resident Evil Veronica release, platform and story updates.
routes.h1: Resident Evil Veronica Sources and Evidence Tracker
routes.intro: The site's key claims are checked against official Capcom announcements, platform storefront records and attributed producer interviews.
body: This tracker follows a strict source hierarchy. Official Capcom announcements and primary product pages carry the most weight for core facts such as the release window, platforms and overall direction.
Steam, the PlayStation Store, the Xbox Store and the Nintendo Store provide platform-specific details such as feature labels, supported languages and wishlist access.
Attributed producer interviews and authorized media coverage add context, but those details remain labeled reported until corroborated by official documentation.

Retailer placeholders, unsourced social claims and screenshots without a source are not confirmation. The Xbox listing currently shows a Mature 17+ badge and content descriptors while also saying the game is not yet rated, so the final age rating remains unresolved.
Verified official video uploads document what was published, and each source is used only for the claim it actually supports.

routes.title: About Veronica Hub: Independent Veronica Tracker
routes.description: Learn who runs Veronica Hub, how the site verifies Resident Evil Veronica information, and how it separates official facts from reported context.
routes.intro: Veronica Hub is an independent fan-made source tracker for Resident Evil Veronica.
body: Veronica Hub exists to help readers follow Resident Evil Veronica without mixing confirmed information, reported context and rumor. The site is independently operated and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by Capcom.

The editorial rule is simple: official facts come from Capcom, official platform stores or verified official video channels. Reported interview details are labeled as reported context. Rumors, retailer placeholders, unsourced screenshots and social reposts are not treated as confirmed information.
The site brings release, platform, PC, trailer and story sources together so readers can check a claim without hunting through several store pages.

Resident Evil, Resident Evil Veronica, Code: Veronica, Capcom and related names are trademarks or property of their respective owners. This site uses those names only to identify the game and discuss publicly available information.

routes.title: Contact Veronica Hub: Corrections and Sources
routes.description: Contact Veronica Hub for corrections, official source changes, attribution questions or site feedback.
routes.intro: Send corrections, source updates and site questions to the Veronica Hub editor.
body: For corrections, source updates, attribution questions or site feedback, email contact@residentevilveronica.com.

Please include the page URL, the specific sentence or item you are referencing, and the official source link that supports the correction. Source-backed corrections are prioritized over speculation or unsourced claims.
For copyright, trademark or media-attribution requests, include the asset URL and the preferred correction. Veronica Hub does not host ROMs, ISOs, cracks, emulators or unofficial downloads.

Useful reports include broken source links, changed official store listings, updated trailer metadata, newly published Capcom pages, incorrect attribution, accessibility issues and pages where an unknown detail should be labeled more clearly.
This contact page is for the independent Veronica Hub site only. For official product support, purchases, account issues or press requests, use Capcom or platform-holder support channels.

routes.title: Privacy Policy for Veronica Hub
routes.description: Privacy policy for Veronica Hub, including analytics, cookies, advertising disclosures and third-party links.
routes.intro: This policy explains what Veronica Hub collects, uses and links to when you visit the site.
body: Veronica Hub is an independent fan-made information site. The site does not ask visitors to create accounts, submit passwords or provide payment information.

The site may use basic analytics to understand page traffic, source-link clicks, trailer plays, language switches, device categories, referrers and performance issues. Analytics data is used to improve navigation, page quality and technical reliability.

The site is configured for Google AdSense. Google and other third-party vendors may use cookies or similar technologies to serve ads based on a visitor's prior visits to this and other websites. Google's advertising cookies enable Google and its partners to serve personalized or non-personalized ads where ads are shown.

Visitors can learn about Google advertising controls and opt out of personalized advertising through Google's Ads Settings. Visitors can also use browser settings or regional privacy tools to limit cookies where available.
Third-party links on this site may lead to Capcom, Steam, YouTube, platform-holder stores, media sites or other external websites. Those websites operate under their own privacy policies and terms.
Contact contact@residentevilveronica.com for privacy questions, correction requests or site-policy questions.

Hardware requirements from nearby RE Engine releases serve strictly as contextual planning references, not as specifications or performance guarantees for Resident Evil Veronica.

Capcom has not confirmed target resolutions, frame rates, CPU models, graphics cards, RAM requirements or installation storage sizes. Ray tracing, upscaling technology and official Steam Deck compatibility also remain unannounced.

routes.title: Resident Evil Veronica: Original vs. Remake Changes
routes.description: Compare the 2000 Code: Veronica with its remake. Track confirmed story adjustments, modernized gameplay and reported developer context.
routes.h1: Resident Evil Veronica Original vs. Remake
routes.intro: Resident Evil Veronica is an official remake of the 2000 classic Code: Veronica, updating the original with modernized gameplay and a reimagined narrative.
body: According to the official Steam listing, the remake retains the core identity of the 2000 release while introducing modernized gameplay, more detailed graphics and a reimagined storyline. PlayStation Blog coverage reports that parts of the original narrative will be adjusted to connect with the broader series lore established since 2000.

Developer interviews report a third-person direction and the involvement of teams behind the Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 4 remakes. The producer also highlighted the original game's importance to the franchise and explained the choice of the shorter Veronica title.

Specific changes to puzzles, campaign structure, combat mechanics, room layouts, item locations, boss sequences and cinematic cutscenes remain unannounced. Returning players should not assume that every original detail carries over unchanged.
New players do not necessarily need to play the original first. The remake's current synopsis provides the essential setup around Claire, Chris, Umbrella and Rockfort Island.

developerPublisherProfile.summary: Resident Evil Veronica lists CAPCOM Co., Ltd. as both developer and publisher on Steam. In practical terms, the developer role covers making the game, including design, engineering, art, audio and production. The publisher role covers commercial release work such as platform coordination, store pages, marketing, localization, age ratings and launch operations. Because Capcom is both developer and publisher here, official Capcom and store channels are especially important sources for factual updates.

faq.question: Is Resident Evil Code Veronica Remake official?
faq.answer: Yes. Capcom announced Resident Evil Veronica for 2027. Official sources describe it as a remake of 2000's Resident Evil Code: Veronica, so the project itself, remake positioning and release window are confirmed rather than rumor.

faq.question: What has Capcom confirmed about the remake itself?
faq.answer: Capcom and Steam describe it as a remake that preserves the essence of the original while adding modernized gameplay, a reimagined storyline and detailed graphics. That confirms direction, but it does not reveal final puzzle design, chapter structure, enemy list or every returning scene.

faq.question: Is Resident Evil Veronica first-person or third-person?
faq.answer: The official trailer includes first-person-looking footage, but producer interview and media Q&A coverage describe the remake as a third-person game. Treat this as reported producer context until Capcom publishes a full gameplay breakdown.

faq.question: Why is it called Resident Evil Veronica instead of Code Veronica?
faq.answer: A producer interview says the team still respects the Code Veronica name, but shortened the remake title to communicate that this story is important like a numbered Resident Evil entry and to align with recent one-word subtitle conventions.

faq.question: Where does the story begin?
faq.answer: Steam places the premise three months after the Raccoon City disaster, with Claire searching for Chris before being captured by Umbrella forces and taken to Rockfort Island. This is the safest spoiler-light setup to repeat because it comes from the current store synopsis.

faq.question: Will the remake change the original story?
faq.answer: Producer Yoshiaki Hirabayashi told PlayStation Blog that parts of the original story will be retuned to connect with the wider Resident Evil lore established since 2000. That confirms a continuity-focused approach, but not which scenes, character arcs or plot details will change.

faq.question: Does Resident Evil Veronica have a final ESRB rating?
faq.answer: Not reliably yet. The Xbox store currently displays a Mature 17+ badge and content descriptors, but the same page still says the content has not yet been age-rated. Until ESRB or Capcom publishes a matching final record, treat the Xbox display as conflicting store metadata rather than a settled final rating.

faq.question: What is the exact release date?
faq.answer: A 2027 release window is confirmed. An exact release date has not been officially confirmed, so day-and-month claims from placeholders, reposts or countdown pages should be treated as unconfirmed unless Capcom or an official platform store publishes them.

faq.question: What platforms are confirmed?
faq.answer: Official sources list PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2 and PC. Steam also has a live store page, which confirms PC store presence and wishlist access but not final PC requirements or price.

faq.question: Are PC system requirements confirmed?
faq.answer: No. Steam lists minimum and recommended system requirements as TBD. PC is confirmed, but exact specs are not official yet, so hardware estimates should be treated as preparation guidance rather than purchase guarantees.

faq.question: Can I use the estimated PC requirements to buy hardware?
faq.answer: Treat the estimate as preparation guidance, not an official purchase guarantee. Wait for Capcom or Steam to publish Resident Evil Veronica requirements before making a final upgrade decision.

faq.question: Is there a demo?
faq.answer: No official demo has been confirmed at the current verification time. A demo would need a Capcom announcement or a live official platform listing before this site treats it as real.

faq.question: Are preorders or editions available?
faq.answer: Wishlist access exists on Steam, but preorder timing, price and editions are not officially confirmed yet. Wishlist buttons should not be confused with preorder checkout, collector editions, deluxe content or physical release plans.

faq.question: Is Veronica Hub an official Capcom site?
faq.answer: No. Veronica Hub is an independent fan-made information site and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Capcom.

referenceGames.title: Resident Evil
referenceGames.storyContext: Established the fixed-camera exploration, puzzles and limited supplies used by the early series.
referenceGames.playability: Deliberate movement, limited inventory space and careful route planning.
referenceGames.whyReference: It shows the survival-horror ideas that later games and remakes keep returning to.
referenceGames.origin: The first Resident Evil established the structure used by the early series.

referenceGames.title: Resident Evil 2
referenceGames.storyContext: Follows Claire and Leon through parallel routes during the Raccoon City outbreak.
referenceGames.playability: Broader routes and more enemies, while limited supplies still make every detour matter.
referenceGames.whyReference: Claire's first game is the most useful early comparison for her role and the series' classic pacing.
referenceGames.origin: Resident Evil 2 expanded the original formula with two protagonists and a larger story.

referenceGames.title: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
referenceGames.storyContext: Builds much of its tension around Jill escaping a recurring pursuer.
referenceGames.playability: Faster movement and frequent chases create more pressure than the first two games.
referenceGames.whyReference: It shows how a recurring threat can change the pace of a Resident Evil campaign.
referenceGames.origin: Resident Evil 3 made Nemesis a constant interruption to exploration.

referenceGames.title: Resident Evil Code: Veronica
referenceGames.storyContext: Continues Claire's search for Chris across Rockfort Island and other locations.
referenceGames.playability: A longer classic-style campaign with fixed cameras, limited supplies and large connected areas.
referenceGames.whyReference: It provides the story, characters and locations that Capcom is now reimagining.
referenceGames.origin: Code: Veronica is the 2000 game that Resident Evil Veronica is remaking.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Established the series' mix of limited supplies, puzzles and slow-building tension.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Set the basic survival-horror structure that later games kept changing.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: The starting point for comparing every later entry.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 2
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Expanded the story with Claire and Leon's parallel routes through Raccoon City.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Made exploration broader while keeping inventory pressure and puzzle-heavy progression.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: Especially relevant because Claire returns in Veronica.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 3: Nemesis
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Made a recurring pursuer central to the campaign.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Added a faster, more relentless kind of tension.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: Useful context for how the series handles chase sequences.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil Code: Veronica
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Continued Claire's search for Chris beyond Raccoon City.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Introduced Rockfort Island and the story now being remade.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: The direct source material for Resident Evil Veronica.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 0
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Added character switching and partner-based puzzles.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Pushed the classic fixed-camera formula toward more complex character management.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: Related design context rather than part of Veronica's direct story.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 4
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Moved the series to an over-the-shoulder camera and faster combat.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Changed how Resident Evil handles movement, aiming and enemy encounters.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: The turning point behind the controls used by the modern remakes.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 5
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Expanded the action focus with co-op and larger combat spaces.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Moved further away from the slower isolation of the early games.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: Useful mainly as a contrast with the remake era.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 6
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Split the game across several protagonists and campaigns.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Took the series' action-heavy direction to its widest scale.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: Helps explain why later games returned to tighter settings.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 7: Biohazard
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Returned the focus to horror through a first-person camera and a smaller setting.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Made close-range exploration and vulnerability central again.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: The beginning of the current RE Engine era.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 2 Remake
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Rebuilt a fixed-camera classic as a modern over-the-shoulder game.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Showed how Capcom can change controls and level flow without losing the original atmosphere.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: The clearest modern comparison for a Code: Veronica remake.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 3 Remake
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Condensed the original into a shorter, faster remake.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Showed that Capcom may change campaign length and structure, not just presentation.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: Relevant when considering how much of Code: Veronica may be reworked.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil Village
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Combined first-person horror with broader areas and more action-heavy bosses.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Shows the larger scale the RE Engine games can support.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: A useful contrast with the tighter recent remakes.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil 4 Remake
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Rebuilt another classic around modern controls, parrying and expanded encounters.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: Shows the current standard for changing combat while preserving a familiar story and tone.
gameHistoryTimeline.note: The newest completed remake to compare with Veronica.

gameHistoryTimeline.title: Resident Evil Veronica Remake
gameHistoryTimeline.event: Capcom confirms the remake for 2027 on PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2 and PC.
gameHistoryTimeline.impact: The question is no longer whether the remake exists, but what Capcom will change.
